active_inquiry.closure_condition: Close when a completed baseline training-and-measurement route yields episode-level success and failure decomposition under the official radius and angle distribution, including time to first entry, entry velocity, maximum consecutive hold, exits, radius and angle conditioning, and branch behavior where available, sufficient to select or reject the leading intervention direction; if the baseline is not measurable, record that bounded result and the specific method-development blocker.
active_inquiry.goal_connection: The human goal requires at least 196 successful complete holds in the fixed 200-episode official assessment. With no candidate or development measurement, mechanism localization is necessary before selecting a recipe or requesting assessment.
active_inquiry.question: Can a baseline policy be trained and measured under the official target distribution well enough to distinguish failure to reach, failure to settle, and failure to maintain the uninterrupted hold, and thereby identify whether the next intervention should target training coverage, motion generation and braking, or hold stabilization?
active_inquiry.rationale: The scientific model establishes that reachability alone is insufficient and identifies three consequential explanations: outer-only training may fail on inner radii, dynamic approach and braking may fail near difficult configurations, or residual motion and discrete sampling may break the hold. No completed operation discriminates among them, so official assessment would be premature and a direct intervention would be speculative. A baseline mechanism-localization inquiry is the smallest goal-linked action that can establish measurable behavior and redirect the campaign using episode-level evidence rather than proxy reward or training completion.

request.current_goal_gap: No policy, development measurement, or official assessment exists, so the campaign has no evidence-backed estimate of episode success and cannot yet distinguish failure to reach, failure to settle, or failure to maintain the hold. The model identifies a structural exposure: training currently samples only the outer official radii [0.14, 0.20] m while assessment samples [0.06, 0.20] m, and outer-radius conditioning may also make stabilization difficult; the behavioral importance of these risks is unmeasured.
request.current_synthesis: Established by the scientific model: the arm is fully observable under fixed-target dynamics, every official target has at least one joint-limit-valid analytic configuration, and success is governed by 100 consecutive post-action samples inside the 1 cm tolerance. These facts make reachability alone insufficient: terminal velocity, local Jacobian conditioning, branch choice, and discrete-time exits can determine complete-hold success. No campaign operation has completed, so there is no observation establishing which mechanism dominates, no evidence that the current PPO recipe learns the official distribution, and no basis for calling any candidate working or best-known. The consequential competing explanations are (1) the outer-only training distribution leaves inner-radius behavior as the main generalization failure, (2) dynamic approach and braking near singular or high-displacement targets prevent settling, or (3) policies can reach targets but fail the uninterrupted hold because residual motion and sampling-time exits are not controlled. These remain hypotheses, not findings.
request.decision_frontier: The next decision is whether to prioritize distribution coverage, motion-generation and braking, or hold-stabilization method development. A discriminating first inquiry should produce episode-level success and failure decomposition under the official radius/angle distribution, including time to first entry, entry velocity, maximum consecutive hold, exits, radius/angle conditioning, and branch behavior; where possible it should also expose actuator saturation and Cartesian speed. Evidence showing inner-radius concentration would support changing training coverage, evidence showing high reach but short holds would support stabilization or reward/control changes, and evidence showing approach failures with velocity or conditioning dependence would support trajectory/braking work. If the initial policy is not yet measurable, a bounded baseline training-and-measurement route must first establish that fact without treating training completion as scientific success.
request.human_goal_connection: The campaign must produce one learned policy with at least 196 successes in the fixed 200-episode official assessment, where every success includes a complete uninterrupted 2-second hold. The initial direction therefore prioritizes identifying the failure mechanism that most threatens complete episode success rather than optimizing a proxy such as reach distance or average hold length.
request.next_direction_or_closure: Enter goal review and select one bounded inquiry directly from the frontier. The most credible first inquiry is baseline mechanism localization: obtain the first evidence-backed policy behavior under the official task distribution and use failure decomposition to choose between coverage, dynamics, and hold-robustness interventions. Do not request official assessment or assign a best-known role before a candidate has completed development evidence.
